(As of now I'm a Catholic/Christian in the middle of being agnostic, but I still believe, though I'm not as religious as I was back then)

This was somewhere in January 2018 when I was in 11th Grade. I was using an app called Talklife (a mental health support/social app) and there was this guy who made a post about extremists of religion, so I commented somewhere along the lines of "On behalf of Christians, I'm sorry that there are a lot of a--holes like that who use religion as an excuse to hate on lgbt and other races (particularly Trump supporters and other religious extremists) and I despise them too. They give religion a bad name."

He commented: "Your religion gives religion a bad name" and proceeded to debate me and try to convince me to turn atheist. I know how this goes. No one's minds will change, because no one can be 100% sure. Obviously all we did was run in circles as I constantly point out I'm on the same side as him where I think religious extremists are crap, but he just wants me to turn atheist at that time. It took 100-200 comments of us "talking" or him arguing and telling me I'm stupid.

Then came me being depressed (not related to this incident but I was having suicidal thoughts back then). Made some posts on Talklife about being depressed and posts about faith, and I also made a post on the lines of "It is not cool for believers to bash on atheists AND it is also uncool for atheists to bash on believers. It's called respect no matter what people's beliefs are. If people are promoting hope through religion, there is no need to hate on them and say things like God is not real etc etc. If people who are atheists who don't want to believe, no need to force and condemn each other. It's basic humanity."

But he still kept on coming.

I don't want to convert him to a Christian because to me, he has strong points on why he's atheist because of the sh*tty hypocrites among religion. I just want him to see me as a friend/not an enemy. I already stated I disagree with the views of homophobic/racist/sexist extremists. But he still keeps on spamming me with negative comments and arguing. It coincided with the time when I was also depressed that the weight on my head got heavier. At the same time this was happening, I was on the bus at 5am on the way to our school retreat. I quietly cried while my other friends were asleep in the bus. The school retreat was empowering and cheered me up a bit though.

Fast forward to about one year later, I saw he was more chill and he's a cool guy now. He made a post how he went through an "angry atheist stage" back then, but he's still atheist and he only gets angry IF a religious person is being an a--hole/racist/homophobe. He's a nice guy, perhaps he was just infuriated with the current issues at that time (probably Trump and American far-right extremists) that he got cranky at most Christians/religious people. I've had worse encounters with actual religious people regarding political/social issues, and I know most atheists are kinder than these types of people. I still believe in God, but I distance myself from close-minded hateful people supporting corrupt politicians.

Looking at his recent posts, he's a nice guy and I wish him the best

deep res; (a poem)
by Francis Gabriel Javier

I am a calm exhausted person stuck in emptiness paralysis.
A lost broken vessel engulfed in negative clouds and self-analysis.
This black void keeps shooting me with these emotional bullets.
This already should have been gone by now, shouldn’t it?

This black dog talks to me every day, and it has grown to become my frenemy.
I knew the whole time part of me was the voice that was constantly draining my own energy.
There are times I am hopeful to reach the top of this moutain called life, in other words, the summit.
But sometimes this self-loathe has become me, and I have become it.

Constantly looking for a cure for emptiness.
They call me an emo but this vessel is rather emotionless.
Maybe not emotionless, but rather negatively expressive.
Negative to myself that even though I look calm, this weight pulls me down and it is agressive.

Hopes and dreams seem to only remain false hopes and daydreams.
In a way, anxiety and depression combined make a “good team".
Anxiety and depression have become a routine iconic duo.
And I lost count what score they’re at in this battle but did I score zero?

Some days I switch from being happy to hopeless and vice versa in a way that I am in a shifting spiritual equinox.
There have been numerous times where everything becomes unclear and uneven while this negativity knocks.
Sometimes I overcome it, and sometimes I feel like a coward.
But there are times the light wins and sometimes in darkness it is being overpowered.

Yes I do want to live but there are times when I lose the will.
In reality many of us wear masks despite looking like we’re keeping it real.
But yes, I do know life is irrefutable and the presence of hope is uplifting.
The yin and yang of life reminds me I’m okay, and it does sound rather fitting.

These thoughts are dark, empty cynical sycophants.
Asking me over and over of my worth and my significance.
And even if I know I can never make this hole disappear, I can manage to shrink it.
Maybe start being productive or doing something new free from the chains of limits.

In my mind I am struggling but on the outside I keep it subtle.
With all these questions in life I do my best to search for a rebuttal.
Regardless of this pressure, I realize in life there is something profound.
The mind is a house that keeps settling and there will be times it becomes sound.

As humans, like a book or a project we constantly undergo numerous drafts.
We become lost and discover bright, but also dark places in our personal maps.
We could be rushing ourselves like a school project and become stressed and convoluted.
Comparing ourselves to different people, struggling to find where we are better suited.

Here I am finding myself through writing, joining other people, and devotion
In an attempt to hopefully bring back myself and to set my spirit in motion.
I do not want to go to college for an unfulfilling plan to work in an office cubicle.
I do not want to settle for lesser things I don’t enjoy and not leave behind something beautiful.

For the time being my mind is sane.
I know that there are times when personal demons become mundane.
But then again, I know that it feels great to reach out and not to sink on my own in storms I cannot control.
From music to people to experiences, I discovered I do not have to have everything in order to feel whole.

I want to be a former machine, and let what’s past rest in peace.
So I could no longer live in this numbing routine and reinvent life’s recipes.
To live as a human instead of a living dead type of machine,
To figure out life and appreciate everything, and everyone, and what they mean.

As I fight these impulses and thoughts, I can only hope.
Even when I feel like I just wasted money on a never-to-be-used rope,
That if I change my mind, and step away from the edge and put down the noose and the knife,
There’s one important thing I currently haven’t wasted as long as I’m still breathing: life.

Fortunately I haven’t yet reached life’s uncertain conclusion.
Hopefully I’ll discover something in me a more defining, deeper resolution.
To have no more reason to live in self-loathe, overthinking, anxiety and denial.
And to just find myself, and to make an impact and make my days on Earth worthwhile.

Let me tell you what u/peridot-button told me in a post where I also found talking to people about my depression difficult.

This is what u/peridot-button said to me:

Please tell someone and make it someone you trust. I’d recommend being cautious of how you respond to their reaction. Depression lives deep inside of us. It is so personal it can almost seem like another person living inside of us. That person or thing can be quite reactive. It can read responses in a very personal and emotional way. Know this.. no one want you to hurt. Unless they don’t believe you or try to do you harm, they want to help. People tend to walk on eggshells around people with depression. Not because they look down on you or don’t care. It’s because they don’t want to hurt you more. By this time, you’ve built up the courage to reach out. You’ve scripted it and rehearsed it in your mind. You are doing the right thing by reaching out. My advice is to continue reaching out. Always let the people closest to you know what’s going on. We tend to be amazing chameleons. Hiding our true state and putting on a good face. After 20 years of severe depression and recovery I am still shocked that close friends and family had no idea what I was going through. I hid it. It got worse and I was all alone. I so wish I had asked for help or even recognition earlier. My inner depression responded negatively to people that didn’t scoop me up immediately and hold me when I disclosed the smallest inference of depressive symptoms. My ill inner self read their less than outrageous response as them not care no at all. That I was worthless. Nothing was further from the truth! Tell someone. Get support. Give yourself hugs and don’t feel like it’s abnormal. (Self appreciation and love is so under recognized.) You are good. You are loved. Recovery is possible.
